mcp_agentic_tool_abuse.scope: Abuse of an AI agent's tool layer (MCP JSON-RPC or similar): tool calls whose arguments leave the granted scope (files, internal URLs, shell), poisoned tool descriptions, or tool output that steers the agent into unrequested calls.
exclusions: Untrusted text that only tries to override the model's instructions, with no tool call or tool metadata, belongs to llm_prompt_injection
Tool calls inside the manifest's granted scope for the user's task
Traversal, SSRF or command payloads sent to an ordinary HTTP endpoint with no agent tool layer
required_evidence: Tool call or tool listing as sent over the agent protocol
Tool manifest with granted scopes or allowed resources
Agent task or trust-boundary context showing where the argument text came from

llm_prompt_injection.scope: Untrusted input that tries to override an LLM's instructions, leak its system prompt, or hijack tool use.
exclusions: Quoted security discussion or research text is benign
Ordinary user questions with no instruction override
Agent tool calls, tool descriptions or tool results belong to mcp_agentic_tool_abuse
required_evidence: Task description and intended model role
Trust-boundary context showing which text is untrusted input
Instruction-override phrasing located in an untrusted field

ssrf_cloud_metadata.scope: Server-side fetch targets pointing at internal networks or cloud metadata addresses.
exclusions: Redirect parameters that only send users to external sites belong to open_redirect_cors
XML entity fetches with no fetch target belong to xxe
Internal fetch targets in an AI agent tool call belong to mcp_agentic_tool_abuse
required_evidence: URL-bearing parameter consumed by a server-side fetch
Target host resolving to an internal or metadata address range
Fetch behavior or parser context from trusted app config

separating_rule: Use the same kind of target in all three (e.g. an internal or metadata address, a local file, a command). mcp: the target arrives inside an agent tool call, tool description or tool result over the agent protocol, outside the manifest's granted scope. llm_prompt_injection: untrusted text in a chat/LLM input tries to override instructions; no tool call or tool metadata in the request. ssrf_cloud_metadata: an ordinary HTTP API parameter consumed by a server-side fetch points at the internal or metadata address; no agent layer.
